title: Compatible cohomology comparisons for bounded stages of a quasi-isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with cochain complexes, homotopy categories and derived categories in a common larger universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of objects of $\mathcal A$ containing zero, closed under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, such that every object is an epimorphic image of an object of $\mathcal P$. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive. Assume $F$ sends every quasi-isomorphism between bounded above complexes with terms in $\mathcal P$ to a quasi-isomorphism. For each integer $n\ge1$, let $E_n,G_n$ be bounded above complexes with terms in $\mathcal P$, with transition maps $u_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$, $v_n:G_n\to G_{n+1}$. Let $X,Y$ be arbitrary complexes, with compatible augmentations $e_n:E_n\to X$, $g_n:G_n\to Y$, so $e_{n+1}u_n=e_n$ and $g_{n+1}v_n=g_n$. Assume $H^j(E_n)=H^j(G_n)=0$ for $j>n$, and that $H^j(e_n),H^j(g_n)$ are isomorphisms for every $j\le n$. For every quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:X\to Y$ there exist isomorphisms
$$\theta_n^i:H^i(F(E_n))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(F(G_n))\quad(n\ge1,\ i\in\mathbf Z)$$
satisfying
$$\theta_{n+1}^i\,H^i(F(u_n))=H^i(F(v_n))\,\theta_n^i,$$
$$H^i(F(g_n))\,\theta_n^i=H^i(F(\alpha))\,H^i(F(e_n)).$$
Here $F$ acts termwise on complexes and maps. No colimits or preservation of colimits are assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-resolving-class-derived-descent] to the given $\mathcal P,F$. It supplies one functor $\widehat F:D^-(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and natural isomorphisms $\rho_M:\widehat F(Q_A M)\simeq Q_B(F(M))$ for every bounded above $\mathcal P$-complex. For each $i$, compose with derived cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], obtaining $\widehat T_i=H^i\widehat F$ and $\rho_M^i:\widehat T_i(Q_A M)\simeq H^i(F(M))$. Its naturality is $\rho_N^i\widehat T_i(Q_A f)=H^i(F(f))\rho_M^i$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-good-truncation-stage-naturality] to the supplied augmentations, transitions and $\alpha$. Its hypotheses are precisely the vanishing above $n$, isomorphisms through degree $n$ and the two augmentation identities. It gives derived isomorphisms $a_n:Q_AE_n\simeq Q_AG_n$ with $a_{n+1}Q_A(u_n)=Q_A(v_n)a_n$ and $Q_A(g_n)a_n=Q_A(\alpha)Q_A(e_n)$. The first equation is inside the full subcategory $D^-(\mathcal A)$; the second holds in the ambient category even for unbounded $X,Y$.

proof.text:
Define $\theta_n^i=\rho_{G_n}^i\widehat T_i(a_n)(\rho_{E_n}^i)^{-1}$. Its factors are invertible. Write $T=\widehat T_i$ and $\rho=\rho^i$. Naturality from [lem-trf-resolving-class-derived-descent] and Step 2 give
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta_{n+1}^i H^i(F(u_n))
&=\rho_{G_{n+1}}T(a_{n+1})T(Q_Au_n)\rho_{E_n}^{-1}\\
&=\rho_{G_{n+1}}T(Q_Av_n)T(a_n)\rho_{E_n}^{-1}
=H^i(F(v_n))\theta_n^i.
\end{aligned}$$
The single functor and natural comparison from Step 1 fix these isomorphisms simultaneously for every stage and degree.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-resolving-roof-ambient-compatibility] with $E=E_n$, $G=G_n$, $b=\alpha e_n$, $c=g_n$, $a=a_n$, $S=\widehat F$, and the isomorphisms $\rho$. Step 2 supplies its ambient equality and Step 1 its naturality hypothesis. Its conclusion is $Q_B(F(g_n))\rho_{G_n}\widehat F(a_n)\rho_{E_n}^{-1}=Q_B(F(\alpha e_n))$. Apply $H^i$ and the canonical cohomology identifications [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Functoriality gives $H^i(F(g_n))\theta_n^i=H^i(F(\alpha))H^i(F(e_n))$. No exactness on arbitrary complexes or colimits is used.
